answer_1.quote: In this paper, we focus on the problem of automatically generating the court's view in civil cases by injecting the plaintiff's claim and fact description, as shown in Fig.
datasets: Civil court view dataset (private lending cases)
answer_1.outputs: Court's view containing judgment and rationales

answer_2.quote: We keep the results of ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L. ... BLEU-1, BLEU-2 to evaluate ... BERT SCORE computes a similarity score by using contextual embedding of the tokens.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation to better analyze the quality of the generated court's view. ... The evaluation is conducted following three perspectives: (1) Judgment level. ... (2) Rational level. ... (3) Fluency level.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators (5 legal experts) score each generated view on three criteria—judgment correctness, rational quality, and fluency—using a 1-5 scale.
